links.outcome: Physician diagnostic accuracy with vs without prompt to judge whether AI list contains correct diagnosis
links.effect: Diagnostic accuracy 41.5% intervention vs 46% control (95% CI -0.75 to 2.55; P=.27); trust calibration correct in only 61.5% of cases.
links.quote: There was no significant intergroup difference in the physicians’ diagnostic accuracy (95% CI −0.75 to 2.55; P =.27).

links.outcome: Whether physicians detect incorrect AI outputs (trust calibration correctness) and overconfidence in AI
links.effect: Trust calibration correct in 61.5% (123/200); accuracy 54.5% when correct vs 20.8% when incorrect; intervention group estimated AI accuracy ~30% higher than actual.
links.quote: The secondary outcome, the correctness of trust calibration in the intervention group, was 61.5% (123/200; Table 2 ).

unlisted_practices: Prompting clinicians to judge whether the correct diagnosis is in the AI differential list (trust calibration) to reduce overreliance
